# Comic ground truth fixtures

Three clean/lettered pairs exercise the native redraw paths, plus the two OCR cards. PNG files allow visual review. Gzipped RGBA files contain the same decoded pixels so Node tests work on Windows and Linux without an image decoder or canvas dependency. `manifest.json` records dimensions, provenance, redistribution terms, grading rectangles, lettering and thresholds.

| Pair | Size | Covers | Provenance and redistribution |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `greenhouse` | 512x768 | White balloon and caption restoration, irregular jacket and coloured glass deferral | Original clean comic art generated with OpenAI ImageGen for this repository; lettering added deterministically with Canvas afterwards. No third-party manga panels or font files. Repository-authored asset, redistributed under the repository terms. |
| `screentone` | 480x640 | Periodic texture path: 8 px period, 3x3 dots at 14% coverage | Generated by `scripts/generate-comic-fixtures.mjs` from repo code and the project's own 5x7 bitmap font. No third-party art or fonts; derivative redistribution is unrestricted. |
| `gradient` | 480x640 | Paper-plane fallback: linear RGB plane with different per-channel slopes | Generated by `scripts/generate-comic-fixtures.mjs` from repo code and the project's own 5x7 bitmap font. No third-party art or fonts; derivative redistribution is unrestricted. |

The English and Japanese OCR cards (`english.png`, `vertical.png`) were rendered with Canvas using Arial and Noto Sans CJK JP; no font files are included.

The white balloon and caption have restoration targets. The caption uses a four-pixel sampling ring contained inside the caption frame. The jacket and greenhouse glass are irregular-background cases. Their preservation checks require the worker to defer when it cannot reliably restore the background. Their remaining lettering error is reported explicitly.

The synthetic pairs are fully opaque (alpha 255) and place their lettering inside rectangles whose sampling ring contains only the target texture or plane, so a grader failure points at the worker instead of the fixture. Ink rules, the panel frame, the shaded block and the circle stay outside every graded rectangle and ring.

## Thresholds

`manifest.json` carries the thresholds and their derivation:

- `maxMae` is the mean absolute channel error over lettered pixels after redraw. The greenhouse pair measured 1.07 on Linux x64 and keeps its original 8. The synthetic pairs measured 0.000 (screentone) and 0.003 (gradient), so they use 4. Unredrawn lettering measures 124-195 MAE, so these limits still fail loudly.
- `thresholds.maxBackgroundChangeRate` is 0.005: at most 0.5% of non-lettered pixels inside a graded rectangle may change by more than 2 levels per channel. Every committed ground-truth run measured exactly 0.
- The two conservative greenhouse cases have no `maxMae`; they carry `maxImprovement: 0.5` instead. The gate fails when their lettering MAE moves by more than 0.5, either way, so a guessed patch cannot pass by improving the error while the worker was supposed to defer.

Raising a threshold requires the measured image difference and an explanation next to the change.

## Regeneration

The synthetic pairs are reproducible from source:

```bash
node scripts/generate-comic-fixtures.mjs         # rewrite screentone/gradient PNG and gzip files
node scripts/generate-comic-fixtures.mjs --check # verify committed pixels still match the generator
```

`npm test` runs the `--check` mode, so a hand-edited synthetic fixture fails the suite.

## Running the benchmark

Run `npm run desktop:native`, then `npm run benchmark -- --output artifacts/benchmark.json`. The report contains the pair id, lettering MAE, unintended background change rate, per-case timing and OCR character error rate. The vertical OCR card requires the Tesseract `jpn_vert` language. Missing language data is recorded in the report. CI requires English on both platforms and installs vertical Japanese on Linux.

These fixtures are a small regression corpus. Add licensed or original examples with their clean reference, lettered input, annotations and provenance to expand coverage. Threshold changes should document the quality tradeoff alongside the image difference.
